items.title: The Twelve Ways a Mind Fails to Be "In Equipoise"

items.zh: 當知此地相略有十二種。或有自性不定故，名非定地。謂五識身。或有闕輕安故，名非定地。謂欲界繫諸心心法。彼心心法，雖復亦有心一境性，然無輕安含潤轉故，不名為定。或有不發趣故，名非定地。謂受欲者，於諸欲中深生染著，而常受用。或有極散亂故，名非定地。謂初修定者，於妙五欲心隨流散。或有太略聚故，名非定地。謂初修定者，於內略心惛睡所蔽。
items.en: Know that the marks of this ground are, in brief, twelve. Some [states] are called non-equipoised because their very nature is unstable — the five sense-consciousnesses. Some are called non-equipoised for lacking pliancy — the minds and mental factors bound to the desire realm; though these also have one-pointedness of a kind, lacking the moistening pervasion of pliancy, they are not called concentration. Some are called non-equipoised for want of any aspiration [to concentration] — those who indulge in desires, deeply defiled by attachment to them and constantly enjoying them. Some are called non-equipoised through extreme scatter — a beginning meditator whose mind still streams out after the five exquisite desires. Some are called non-equipoised through excessive contraction — a beginning meditator whose inwardly-narrowed mind is overcome by dullness and sleep.

items.zh: 或有未證得故，名非定地。謂初修定者，雖無散亂及以略聚、嬈惱其心，然猶未得諸作意故，諸心心法不名為定。或有未圓滿故，名非定地。謂雖得作意，然未證得加行究竟及彼果故，不名為定。或有雜染污故，名非定地。謂雖證得加行究竟果作意，然為種種愛味等惑染污其心。或有不自在故，名非定地。謂雖已得加行究竟果作意，其心亦無煩惱染污，然於、入、住出諸定相中，未得自在，未隨所欲，硬澁艱難。或有不清淨故，名非定地。謂雖自在，隨其所欲、無澁無難，然唯修得世間定故，未能永害煩惱隨眠諸心心法，未名為定。或有起故，名非定地。謂所得定雖不退失，然出定故，不名為定。或有退故，名非定地。謂退失所得三摩地故，不名為定。
items.en: Some are non-equipoised for not yet having attained [genuine absorption]: a beginning meditator who, though free of scatter or excessive contraction, has not yet attained any of the [seven] attentions, so his minds and mental factors are not yet called concentration. Some are non-equipoised for being not yet complete: though attention is attained, the consummation of means and its fruit are not yet realised. Some are non-equipoised through defilement: though the fruit of the consummation of means is attained, the mind is still stained by relish and similar afflictions. Some are non-equipoised for lacking mastery: though free of such afflictions, one has not yet gained ease in entering, abiding in, and emerging from the concentration-states, still meeting resistance and difficulty. Some are non-equipoised for lacking purity: though mastery is gained, only a worldly concentration has been cultivated, unable to permanently destroy the latent afflictions. Some are non-equipoised simply through having emerged: though the concentration attained has not been lost, one has left it, and so it is not, at this moment, called concentration. And some are non-equipoised through retrogression: the concentration once attained has been lost, and so is not called concentration.

items.title: Another Major Threshold: Two Grounds at Once — With-Mind and Without-Mind

items.zh: 已說非三摩呬多地。云何有心地？云何無心地？謂此二地，俱由五門應知其相。一、地施設建立門，二、心亂不亂建立門，三、生不生建立門，四、分位建立門，五、第一義建立門。
items.en: The Grounds With-Mind and Without-Mind, the eighth and ninth in the Basic Section. The Ground of Non-Equipoise has now been explained. What is the Ground With-Mind? What is the Ground Without-Mind? These two grounds should both be known through five gateways: the gateway of establishing them by the [seventeen] grounds, the gateway of establishing them by whether the mind is disturbed or undisturbed, the gateway of establishing them by whether [mind] arises or does not arise, the gateway of establishing them by stage, and the gateway of establishing them by ultimate meaning.

items.title: Gateway One Completes: Which Grounds Are With-Mind, Which Are Without

items.zh: 地施設建立者，謂五識身相應地、意地、有尋有伺地、無尋唯伺地、此四一向是有心地。無尋無伺地中，除無想定并無想生及滅盡定，所餘一向是有心地。若無想定、若無想生、及滅盡定，是無心地。
items.en: As for establishing them by the [seventeen] grounds: the Ground Correlated with the Five Sense-Consciousness-Bodies, the Mind Ground, the Ground With Applied and Sustained Thought, and the Ground Without Applied but With Only Sustained Thought — these four are entirely the Ground With-Mind. Within the Ground Without Applied or Sustained Thought, apart from the no-perception attainment, together with rebirth as one without perception, and the cessation attainment, the remainder is entirely the Ground With-Mind. The no-perception attainment, rebirth as one without perception, and the cessation attainment are the Ground Without-Mind.

items.title: Gateway Two: Disturbed Mind and Undisturbed Mind

items.zh: 心亂不亂建立者，謂四顛倒顛倒其心，名為亂心。若四顛倒不顛倒心，名不亂心。此中亂心，亦名無心，性失壞故。如世間見心狂亂者，便言此人是無心人。由狂亂心失本性故。於此門中，諸倒亂心，名無心地。若不亂心，名有心地。
items.en: As for establishing them by whether the mind is disturbed or undisturbed: a mind inverted by the four inversions is called a disturbed mind. A mind not inverted by the four inversions is called an undisturbed mind. Here, a disturbed mind is also called no-mind, because its very nature has been ruined. It is like the world's way of speaking, on seeing someone whose mind is deranged, of calling that person "mindless" — because the deranged mind has lost its original nature. Through this gateway, every mind inverted and disturbed by the [four inversions] is called the Ground Without-Mind. An undisturbed mind is called the Ground With-Mind.

items.title: Gateway Three: The Eight Conditions Governing Whether Mind Arises

items.zh: 生不生建立者，八因緣故，其心或生，或復不生。謂根破壞故，境不現前故，闕作意故、未得故、相違故、已斷故、已滅故、已生故、心不得生。由此相違諸因緣故，心乃得生。此中若具生因緣故，心便得生，名有心地。若遇不生心因緣故，心則不生，名無心地。
items.en: As for establishing them by whether [mind] arises or does not arise: owing to eight conditions, mind either arises or fails to arise. Namely: because the [sense] faculty is impaired; because the object is not present; because attention is lacking; because [the capacity] has not been attained; because [a contrary condition] is opposed [to it]; because [the afflictive condition] has already been cut off; because [its seed] has already been extinguished; because [that very moment of mind] has already arisen — for these reasons, mind fails to arise. When these conditions are reversed, mind is then able to arise. Here, when the conditions for arising are complete and mind is thereby able to arise, this is called the Ground With-Mind. When one meets the conditions for mind's non-arising, so that mind does not arise, this is called the Ground Without-Mind.

items.title: Gateway Four: The Six Named Occasions of No-Mind

items.zh: 分位建立者，謂除六位，當知所餘名有心地。何等為六？謂無心睡眠位、無心悶絕位、無想定位、無想生位、滅盡定位、及無餘依涅槃界位。如是六位，名無心地。
items.en: As for establishing them by stage: apart from six stages, know that the remainder is called the Ground With-Mind. What are the six? Namely: the stage of mindless sleep, the stage of mindless fainting, the stage of the no-perception attainment, the stage of rebirth as one without perception, the stage of the cessation attainment, and the stage of the nirvāṇa-realm without residue. These six stages are called the Ground Without-Mind.

items.title: The Fifth Gateway, and a Final Section: With-Mind and Without-Mind Close Entirely

items.zh: 第一義建立者，謂唯無餘依涅槃界中，是無心地。何以故？於此界中，阿賴耶識亦永滅故。所餘諸位，轉識滅故，名無心地。阿賴耶識未永滅盡，於第一義非無心地。
items.en: As for establishing them by ultimate meaning: only within the nirvāṇa-realm without residue is it the Ground Without-Mind. Why is this? Because within this realm, the ālaya-vijñāna, too, has permanently ceased. In the remaining stages, it is only the transforming consciousnesses that have ceased, [and on that basis] they are called the Ground Without-Mind; the ālaya-vijñāna has not yet permanently and completely ceased, so in the ultimate sense they are not the Ground Without-Mind.

items.title: A Major Threshold: The Ground With-Mind and Without-Mind Closes, and the Ground of What Is Attained Through Hearing Opens

items.zh: 已說有心無心地。云何聞所成地？謂若略說，於五明處名句文身無量差別，覺慧為先，聽聞、領受、讀誦、憶念。又於依止名身、句身、文身義中，無倒解了。如是名為聞所成地。
items.en: The Ground of What Is Attained Through Hearing, the tenth, part one, in the Basic Section. The Grounds With-Mind and Without-Mind have now been explained. What is the Ground of What Is Attained Through Hearing? Briefly stated: with respect to the boundless distinctions among the name-bodies, phrase-bodies, and letter-bodies of the five sciences, [one develops], with innate discernment leading the way, the [activities of] listening, receiving, reciting, and remembering. Furthermore, with respect to the meanings that depend on those name-bodies, phrase-bodies, and letter-bodies, one comes to understand them without inversion. This is called the Ground of What Is Attained Through Hearing.

blocks.text: Day 100. Today the treatise covers three of the seventeen stages in a single reading: the seventh, **non-equipoise**, and the eighth and ninth together, the stages **with mind** and **without mind**. They are short because most of their content has already been covered; these stages sort what we know into new categories. The last passage reaches one of Yogācāra's central claims: only in final nirvāṇa does mind truly cease.

A mind fails to be "in equipoise" in twelve ways. The five sense consciousnesses are non-equipoised "because their very nature is unstable". Desire-realm minds have some one-pointedness, but, Master Cháng Bǎi explains, without at least threshold concentration there is no pliancy and bliss, so they do not count. Others are non-equipoised "for want of any aspiration": Venerable Miào Jìng: "to study concentration you must leave desire, but he refuses." Others through "retrogression". Venerable Miào Jìng's example is unexpected: "being a peacemaker, with good intentions, and losing your own concentration". Master Cháng Bǎi adds long journeys and long illness.

The eighth and ninth stages are explained together through five gateways. Which grounds have mind? The five sense consciousnesses, the mind stage, the three grounds of thought, and others. Which are "without mind"? Only certain states, below.
A mind may be disturbed (by the inversions) or undisturbed.

subs.head: Eight conditions for mind not arising

blocks.text: Mind does not arise when the faculty is impaired, the object absent, attention lacking, the capacity not yet attained, an opposing state present, the affliction already cut off, the mind already extinguished, or the mind not yet born. Venerable Miào Jìng distinguishes two: "cut off" means greed, hatred, and delusion no longer arising after the noble path; "extinguished" is like the no-perception attainment.

The stages without mind: **mindless sleep**, **mindless fainting** (Day 4), the **attainment without perception**, **rebirth without perception**, the **attainment of cessation** (Day 94), and **nirvāṇa without remainder**.

"In the ultimate sense, only nirvāṇa without remainder is called without mind, because there the ālayavijñāna too ceases." In the other five, only the six active consciousnesses stop; the ālayavijñāna continues, which is why one can wake, revive, or emerge (Day 94).

Who enters final nirvāṇa? Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only fixed-lineage two-vehicle beings: arhats and pratyekabuddhas who will never arouse the bodhi-mind." And he adds, citing the *Laṅkāvatāra*, that such beings are "drunk on the wine of samādhi; when it wears off, they awaken" and continue towards Buddhahood. The Mahāyāna reading: even final nirvāṇa is a pause, not an end.

"The Ground With Mind and Without Mind has been explained." With fascicle 13's last third, the treatise begins the tenth stage, the **Stage Attained Through Hearing** (聞所成地), which opens the second group of stages: practice.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, why are the five sense-consciousnesses non-equipoised?
options: because their very nature is unstable
quiz.why: "Know that the marks of this ground are, in brief, twelve. Some are called non-equipoised because their very nature is unstable — the five sense-consciousnesses." Master Cháng Bǎi: this ground means lacking threshold concentration, completeness, or mastery — the scattered state.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "non-equipoised for want of any aspiration"?
options: to cultivate concentration one must leave desire, but he won't, so he can't
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "To study concentration you must leave desire, but he refuses to leave desire, so he can't cultivate it." The text: those who indulge desires, deeply attached, constantly enjoying them.

quiz.q: "Non-equipoised through retrogression." What does Venerable Miào Jìng give as a cause of losing concentration?
options: playing peacemaker — kindly mediating disputes — and losing one's own concentration; also long journeys, long illness, much recitation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Being a peacemaker, with good intentions — and losing your own concentration." Master Cháng Bǎi likewise: mediating disputes or exhaustion makes one lose concentration.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what eight conditions prevent mind from arising?
options: impaired faculty, absent object, lacking attention, not yet attained, opposed, already cut off, already extinguished, already arisen
quiz.why: "Because the faculty is impaired; because the object is not present; because attention is lacking; because the capacity has not been attained; because a contrary condition is opposed; because it has already been cut off; because it has already been extinguished; because it has already arisen — for these reasons, mind fails to arise." Venerable Miào Jìng: capable people have strong attention.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the six stages of no-mind?
options: mindless sleep, mindless fainting, no-perception attainment, rebirth without perception, cessation, and nirvāṇa without residue
quiz.why: "The stage of mindless sleep, the stage of mindless fainting, the stage of the no-perception attainment, the stage of rebirth as one without perception, the stage of the cessation attainment, and the stage of the nirvāṇa-realm without residue." Master Cháng Bǎi: mindless sleep is deep, dreamless sleep.

quiz.q: In the ultimate sense, only nirvāṇa without residue is no-mind, since the ālaya ceases. Who enters it, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: only the fixed-lineage two-vehicle beings — arhats and pratyekabuddhas who never turn to the Mahāyāna
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only fixed-lineage two-vehicle beings — fixed arhats and pratyekabuddhas who will never arouse the great aspiration." Maitreya states firmly that "the ālaya too has permanently ceased." The note's generic "arhat" is too broad.

quiz.q: What does the Laṅkāvatāra say of two-vehicle beings entering nirvāṇa, as Venerable Miào Jìng cites?
options: they are "drunk on the wine of samādhi; when it wears off, they awaken"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The *Laṅkāvatāra* says two-vehicle beings in nirvāṇa without remainder are 'drunk on the wine of samādhi; when it wears off they awaken.'" He also cites Yinshun's *Āgama*-based view that they are extinguished. Master Cháng Bǎi cites Kuiji on transformation-śrāvakas.
